knowledge_delta.summary: Pydantic AI adds a typed application-boundary model for agent outputs, dependencies, tools and behavioral evaluation. Existing ReAct/controlled-execution/history concepts are suppressed because typing is narrower than those reasoning or production-control responsibilities.

items.label: Typed agent contract
items.source_basis: The repository emphasizes typed structured outputs and a typed agent API.
items.prior_basis: Existing graph concepts describe reasoning, orchestration and governance but not a schema-validated application contract around an agent result.
items.interpretation: Typing turns model output into an explicit runtime boundary for downstream code without claiming semantic correctness.

items.label: RunContext dependency injection
items.source_basis: RunContext carries typed dependencies into tools/instructions during an agent run.
items.prior_basis: The graph has execution/runtime concepts but no general agent-application concept for explicit typed dependency injection.
items.interpretation: Runtime services and context become inspectable application dependencies rather than hidden global state.

items.label: Validated tool boundary
items.source_basis: Tool signatures/docstrings form schemas and arguments are validated before tool code runs.
items.prior_basis: Existing controlled-execution concepts govern consequential work more broadly; they do not represent this code-level schema boundary.
items.interpretation: Tool validation reduces structural interface errors but does not supply authorization or side-effect safety by itself.

items.label: Agent evaluation surface
items.source_basis: The repository positions Pydantic Evals as a dedicated way to test agent behavior, alongside OpenTelemetry instrumentation.
items.prior_basis: Replayable evaluation in the existing graph is specifically historical execution replay and should not be reused for a generic eval framework.
items.interpretation: Behavioral evaluation remains a separate quality layer after type correctness is established.

claims.text: Pydantic AI positions its core as a typed extensible agent loop with typed structured outputs and dependencies.

evidence.locator: README → opening product definition / Why Pydantic AI

claims.text: Pydantic AI derives tool schemas from Python functions and validates tool arguments before application tool code runs.
RunContext carries typed runtime dependencies into agent tools and instructions during execution.
Pydantic AI exposes evaluation and instrumentation as separate quality/observability surfaces rather than treating typed output as evidence that agent behavior is correct.

evidence.locator: README → Why Pydantic AI → Measured, not vibes

claims.note: This is the project's architecture interpretation of the repository's separate typing, instrumentation and eval surfaces.

prerequisite_map.summary: The model needs four related boundaries: typed result contracts, explicit RunContext dependencies, validated tools and a separate behavioral evaluation surface.

items.label: Typed agent contract
items.reason: The central value disappears if typed output is treated as only developer ergonomics rather than a runtime application boundary.

items.label: RunContext dependency injection
items.reason: Explicit dependencies explain how tools receive application services and data without hiding them in global state or prompts.

items.label: Validated tool boundary
items.reason: Tool schema validation is the concrete boundary where model-generated arguments enter application code.

items.label: Agent evaluation surface
items.reason: Type correctness cannot establish behavioral quality, so a separate eval surface is needed to complete the model.

learning_prompt.retention_prompt: Without looking back, reconstruct the Pydantic AI application boundary: what becomes typed, how RunContext carries dependencies, what is validated before a tool runs, and which production/quality concerns still require separate controls or evals?

transfer_prompt.prompt: An agent prepares a customer update using a typed output model and a typed tool. Which failures can those contracts prevent, what belongs in RunContext, and which authorization or side-effect controls must still live outside this typed SDK boundary?

source_decision.rationale: The explainer preserves the typed-boundary mental model, but the README examples are worth a targeted skim because they show output_type, RunContext and tool validation in a small amount of code. Provider/capability catalogs are not required for the current goal.

novelty.reason: The source adds explicit typed agent-application boundaries not represented as standalone concepts in the current graph.

source_quality.reason: The official repository is the primary source for the framework's API/positioning and is version-bounded to v2.35.1.

relevance.reason: Typed outputs, dependencies and tools are directly applicable to building reliable Python agent applications.

practical_leverage.reason: The model can immediately change how agent tools and downstream result handling are implemented.

compression_loss.reason: The core model compresses well, but the short code examples are useful for seeing exactly where validation and RunContext enter execution.
